reason: Letting makers set tasks and pause machines addresses the earlier problem of lost control and may lead toward sharing necessary work.
expectation: I expect a proposal for greater worker control, though it may not yet address how demanding care is shared.

effect: The workshop design specifies practical decision rights, but does not yet address how demanding work is shared.
reaction: The distinction between community ownership and actual worker control is useful.
reason: Choosing work for skill and pleasure directly explores different possibilities for a good working life.
expectation: I expect an account of work chosen for enjoyment and skill, though it may not resolve who does necessary care.

effect: Valuing skill and experience does not make every necessary task enjoyable, so the remaining demanding work needs attention.
reaction: That qualification makes the workshop proposal more credible.
reason: Compare the attractive work with demanding tasks to address how necessary care is shared.

effect: The comparison leaves care and maintenance as necessary work requiring support and sharing, rather than resolving who does it.
reaction: The unresolved burden is a useful qualification to the workshop ideal.
reason: The only available combination compares prosperity and good lives with the makers' control over their work.
expectation: I expect a discussion of how control over work relates to a good life, without assuming everyone wants the same thing.

effect: The final comparison distinguishes prosperity from a single prescribed good life and completes the chapter.
reaction: The conclusion is clear, though it says little about how maker control supports different choices.

mostWorthwhile.text: The comparison with demanding care and maintenance was most worthwhile: it tested the appealing workshop ideal against work that still needs support and sharing.

leastWorthwhile.text: The final comparison felt least satisfying: its conclusion about different good lives was sensible but did not explain much about the role of maker control.

surprise.text: The workshop design distinguished community ownership from actual rights to choose tasks and stop unsafe work.

arbitrary.text: The connection between maker decision rights and the broad conclusion about a prosperous city felt somewhat indirect.

continue.text: I would probably continue: the chapter's practical qualifications about control and care make me curious how later proposals would handle those tensions.
